<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6422da58e83ac5032030c7daa4787fddf5eeb165` → `packageMentionDocs`.

```sh

git fetch origin be076954b9d126671f9873159a2eb4f807d5f837 && git checkout be076954b9d126671f9873159a2eb4f807d5f837
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6422da58e83ac5032030c7daa4787fddf5eeb165 01f606f4b8101cd53d2e93c95d8de97cd549167e && git checkout -B drift-repro 6422da58e83ac5032030c7daa4787fddf5eeb165 && git merge --no-ff 01f606f4b8101cd53d2e93c95d8de97cd549167e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6422da58e83ac5032030c7daa4787fddf5eeb165
```

</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than

> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6422da58e83ac5032030c7daa4787fddf5eeb165` → pass the list as

### ① Derived judgments

Diff read as `git diff a31ff2eb5..01f606f4b` (the merge base with `main`): 11 files, +285 / −6, identical to the PR's file list.

1. **The declared accept-set narrowing — right.** A `sys_comment` insert or update whose `thread_id` names `sys_organization`, `sys_team`, `sys_business_unit` or `sys_user` is now refused. Read in `audit-writers.ts`: `enforceFeedsCapability` (:2218–:2233) takes the object off `thread_id`, resolves it through `getObjectDef` → `engine.getSchema` (:1338), and throws `code: FEEDS_DISABLED`, `status: 403`, `object` when `def?.enable?.feeds === false`; it is registered on both `beforeInsert` and `beforeUpdate` for `sys_comment` (:2234–:2235). The four definitions now carry `feeds: false` in their `enable:` blocks and nothing else in those files moves. The gate itself is untouched by the PR; the narrowing is entirely the metadata flip, at the one hook seam every caller crosses (REST, SDK, engine), as the changeset says.
2. **The grandfather half — right.** On update an absent `thread_id` returns before the check (:2219–:2222), so a body edit on a stored row still saves; the read path carries no feeds gate at all — `comment-access-hooks.ts` never reads `enable.feeds` (its own header, :84, calls the two gates orthogonal). "Comments already stored are kept and stay readable" holds.
3. **The public-surface change in `@objectstack/platform-objects` — right.** `enable.feeds: false` on four exported definitions, served through `/meta/object`. The key is valid and means what the PR says: `ObjectCapabilities.feeds` is `z.boolean().default(true)` on a strict object (`object.zod.ts` :302; opt-out contract :214–:226), precedent `sys-comment-reaction.object.ts` :138. No `packages/spec` change, no generated spec artefact owed, no governed path in the diff.
4. **The console consumer — right, read at the PIN.** `.objectui-sha` is `daeb77fc…` on the head and on `origin/main` (the PR does not move it). At that sha `RecordDetailView.tsx:1754` reads `objectDef?.enable?.feeds !== false` and `:3284` prunes the Discussion nodes from the rendered page; `activitiesEnabled` is a separate read, so the activity timeline is untouched, as the changeset states. The PR cites `63d00da`, a descendant of the pin carrying the same lines — fine, but the pin is the reading `Console Pin Gate` builds.
5. **No platform producer is broken — right.** At the head no non-test code creates `sys_comment` outside plugin-audit's own hooks; no thread literal naming one of the four objects exists under `packages/qa`, `examples`, or in objectui's tests (objectui names `sys_user` only in activity-roster tests). The dogfood comment fixtures use their own `cmt_*` objects.
6. **The pins — right, and they pin the composition rather than the gate.** `identity-objects-feeds-off.test.ts` imports the REAL four definitions through the already-registered `@objectstack/platform-objects/identity` → `src` alias (`vitest.config.ts`, the #21197 entry), boots a real `ObjectQL`, and installs the real `installAuditWriters(engine, packageId)` (:1124). Per object: `code` + `status` + `object` asserted and no row lands; grandfathered row: the gate is shown live on the same thread first, then the stored row reads back and a body edit saves; a CONTROL business object still accepts a comment. The file is in `tsconfig.test.json`'s program (`TypeScript Type Check` green). The generic gate stays pinned in `audit-writers.test.ts` and `capability-gate-update-verb.test.ts`. The ablation table in the PR body is the dev's claim and was not re-run here; the CI-run pins are the verdict.
7. **The `sys_comment.thread_id` example swap — right.** `sys_user:abc123` → `account:9001` in `sys-comment.object.ts` :10 and :129; the `en` bundle regenerated (AGENTS.md: `en` is rewritten from source), the zh-CN / ja-JP / es-ES leaf VALUES swapped by hand (permitted: editing a translated string is fine, no key added or dropped). `git grep sys_user:abc123` at the head: 0 hits outside CHANGELOGs; none of the four drift-listed docs restates the example. The shipped example no longer prescribes a request this PR refuses.
8. **The code comments citing `objectui#12614 item 1`** in the four `enable:` blocks are code comments beside neighbours citing `#1591` / `#3543` — not runtime strings, not rule text. Not a defect.

The body does not name the example swap; it changes one description's example and no behaviour, and the PR body's acceptance notes record it. Noted; not a condition of this verdict.

- **`Clause-②:` — right.** `no (narrowing: the comment create door refuses on four platform objects that accept it today)` on the PR body and in the changeset, byte-identical. `clause2-line.mjs` `readArmToken` (:286) reads the first token inside the parenthetical, and the `:` after it is neither a word character nor `|`, so the arm is `narrowing` (the docblock at :244–:248 says exactly this). `no` is truthful: no accept set widens.
